narrative: Material PL1__M1AFA50A exhibits smooth, near-continuous demand averaging 545.7 units per working day with a CV of 39.6%, well-suited to a classical (r,Q) replenishment policy anchored on the Economic Order Quantity. A statistically significant upward trend (+1.29 units/day, p=0.010) was detected, indicating the policy should be recalibrated at least quarterly. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=31.6%, mean 4.24 days) after removing one extreme data-entry outlier (9,201.55 days); this variability is the primary driver of the recommended safety stock of 1,407 units, which is 85% above the current SAP level of 759 units and properly calibrated for a 95% service level.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) continuous-review reorder-point with fixed EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth (CV<0.5) with a non-zero fraction of 99.2%, ruling out intermittent-demand models such as Croston. The near-normal distribution and stable (if slightly variable) lead times satisfy the assumptions of the classical (r,Q) model. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs optimally given the high unit volume.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (peak inventory 7,300 vs. limit 9,954; 73.3% utilisation). The upward demand trend may erode the safety stock buffer over time if not recalibrated — the primary service risk is trend-driven demand growth outpacing the fixed policy.
